messages.subject: issue with data and analysis
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am using DISTANCE 6.2. I have data for Nilgai population density. As the population is scanty in my study area, I have a lot of zeros in my data i.e. there are many observations of transects in which I did not detect any animal. It shows errors like "two or more zeros are detected" And therefore the analysis remains erroneous. It asks to replace all zeros with -1.0. My queries are:
1) By replacing 0 with -1, does it mean that the observations are not taken for analysis?
2) If I replace only cluster sizes by zero with -1 and keep the distances zero itself, what difference will it make in analysis.
3) If I remove all the zeros it will reduce my sample size.

What to do??

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] issue with data and analysis
parts:
Abhijeet

I see you are studying this large antelope (nilgai) and that the population density is low so there are transects on which you see no animals.

In this situation, you enter the transect length, but nothing else for that record.  You do not enter the perpendicular distance as zero, nor do you enter the cluster size as zero.  You merely leave those fields in the record blank.

In your message, you seem to have confused transects with no sightings with sightings for which cluster size was not recorded.  It is when cluster size was not recorded that the "-1" is used.  But that is not your situation.

Here are some imaginary data where two species were observed showing how to create a file to be imported into Distance.  There are 7 fields in this dataset; in order (left to right): stratum label, stratum area, transect label, transect length, species, perpendicular distance, cluster size:

L1-09, 500, L1-T1, 200, S1, 2, 3
L1-09, 500, L1-T1, 200, S2, 12, 6
L1-09, 500, L1-T2, 300,,,
L1-09, 500, L1-T3, 400, S1, 4, 12
L1-09, 500, L1-T3, 400, S1, 13, 4
L1-09, 500, L1-T3, 400, S2, 10, 2
...
L1-10, 500, L1-T1, 200, S1, 14, 1
L1-10, 500, L1-T2, 300, S1, 5, 3
L1-10, 500, L1-T2, 300, S2, 4, 6
L1-10, 500, L1-T3, 400, S2, 5, 4
L1-10, 500, L1-T4, 500, S1, 1, 2
...
L2-09, 800, L2-T1, 900, S1, 3, 4
L2-09, 800, L2-T2, 300, S2, 3, 1
....

The ... indicate there are additional rows I did not show.  Note particularly record 3, which is important in your situation.  It shows transect 2 in stratum L1-09.  The transect was 300 units in length, but no detections were made.  Hence the fields for species, perpendicular distance and cluster size are all BLANK, yet the commas are still present to indicate the fields exist but contain blanks (NOT zeroes).
